title: About Luminary Health
content:
Luminary Health is transforming radiology with AI-powered clinical decision support that helps radiologists deliver faster, more accurate diagnoses.

Founded in 2023 by Dr. Anika Sharma and Ben Torres, Luminary Health was born from a simple observation: radiologists are overwhelmed. With imaging volumes growing 5-10% annually and a worsening shortage of trained radiologists, the gap between demand and capacity is widening every year.

Our platform integrates directly into existing PACS workflows, providing real-time AI-assisted analysis that reduces read times by up to 40% without sacrificing diagnostic accuracy. We prioritize cases by urgency, flag critical findings automatically, and give radiologists a trusted second opinion on every scan.

Luminary Health is trusted by over 180 hospitals and health systems across the United States. Our technology has analyzed more than 2 million studies, helping clinicians catch findings that might otherwise be delayed or missed.

Backed by Sequoia and AIVC, our team of 45 combines deep expertise in machine learning, medical imaging, and clinical workflow design. We are headquartered in San Francisco with a growing distributed engineering team.

We are expanding beyond radiology into cardiology and other imaging-intensive specialties, with the goal of becoming the AI layer that supports every diagnostic imaging decision.

Learn more at luminaryhealth.com or contact us at hello@luminaryhealth.com.

title: Luminary Health — Q1 2026 Board Meeting Notes

Board Meeting — Luminary Health
March 18, 2026 | 10:00 AM PT | Zoom

Attendees: Anika Sharma (CEO), Ben Torres (CTO), Mia Chen (VP Product), David Okonkwo (AIVC, Board), Sarah Chen (AIVC, observer this meeting), Elena Rodriguez (AIVC)

- Runway: ~16 months at current burn. Not urgent but we need to start thinking about Series B positioning for late 2026 / early 2027
- Headcount: 42 (added 3 engineers, 1 clinical specialist in Q1)

## Product Update (Ben / Mia)
- Core radiology platform stable, v3.2 shipped in Feb with improved chest X-ray model (sensitivity up 4 pts)
- Cardiology module: early prototype stage, Ben demoed internally. Using transfer learning from radiology models. Targeting beta with 3-5 hospital partners in Q3 2026
- FDA 510(k) for cardiology — Anika says 6-9 month timeline once we submit, planning submission in Q4
- Mia flagged need for more clinical validation data for cardiology. Wants to partner with an academic medical center

## Mayo Clinic Conversation
- Anika shared that she's been in discussions with Mayo Clinic's radiology innovation team since January
- They ran a pilot with 500 studies in Feb — results were strong (38% read time reduction, 99.2% concordance with radiologist reads)
- Mayo is interested in a broader deployment. Anika expects LOI by end of April, full contract by May
- This would be a marquee reference customer — huge for Series B story
- David: emphasized importance of nailing the rollout. Asked Anika to keep board updated on timeline

## Hiring Discussion
- VP Sales: CRITICAL gap. Anika is still doing most of the enterprise selling herself. She's stretched thin between CEO duties, medical evangelism (conferences, publications, Mayo relationship), and closing deals
- David raised this as the #1 priority. We need someone who understands health system procurement cycles and can build a repeatable sales motion
- Anika agreed but said she's struggled to find candidates who understand both enterprise sales and healthcare. Two candidates fell through in Q4
- ACTION: David to send Anika 3-4 VP Sales candidates from AIVC network. Elena to research healthcare sales recruiting firms
- Engineering: need 2 more ML engineers for cardiology team. Ben says he has good pipeline from Google Health alumni network
- Robert Kim (Head of Partnerships) is performing well — landed 3 new health system integrations in Q1

## Competitive Landscape
- Aidoc continues to be the main competitor. They have more funding ($200M+ total raised) and broader product suite
- Viz.ai is strong in stroke/neuro but rumored to be working on cardiac imaging — potential conflict with our cardiology plans
- Anika's view: our advantage is workflow integration and radiologist UX. Competitors focus on detection accuracy, we focus on fitting into how radiologists actually work

## Action Items
1. David: VP Sales candidate intros by end of March
2. Elena: research healthcare sales recruiting firms — report back by April 1
3. Anika: Mayo Clinic update by mid-April
4. Ben: cardiology demo for AIVC team at April product review

title: Luminary Health — Product Demo Day Notes (Cardiology Module)
author: Elena Rodriguez
content:
Product Demo — Luminary Health Cardiology Prototype
April 10, 2026 | 2:00 PM PT | Zoom

Ben and Mia walked me through the cardiology prototype. This was the demo David asked Ben to set up at the March board meeting.

## What I Saw
- They demoed the echocardiogram analysis module running on a test dataset of ~200 studies from a partner hospital (anonymized)
- The AI identifies structural abnormalities, measures ejection fraction automatically, and flags potential valve issues
- UI is clean — same design language as the radiology product. Mia said they're reusing 70% of the frontend components
- Processing time: ~45 seconds per study, which Ben says will come down to <20 seconds with optimization

## Technical Impressions
- Ben explained the transfer learning approach: they're using feature extractors trained on their radiology image corpus and fine-tuning on cardiac imaging data
- He seemed confident about the technical path. Said the hard part isn't the model — it's getting enough labeled training data for cardiac edge cases
- They're working with a cardiologist advisor (Dr. James Liu at UCSF) who is providing expert labeling and clinical validation
- Ben mentioned they need to get to 10,000 labeled studies to feel confident about accuracy. Currently at ~3,000

## Product Strategy (Mia)
- Mia's plan is to launch cardiology as an add-on module for existing radiology customers first
- Pricing: $2-3K/month per site on top of existing radiology contract
- She estimates 30-40% of current customers have cardiology imaging departments that could adopt
- The expansion play is smart — land with radiology, expand to cardiology, eventually cover all imaging

## My Take
- I'm genuinely impressed. The prototype is further along than I expected. The radiology-to-cardiology transfer learning approach gives them a real speed advantage over competitors building cardiac AI from scratch
- The data labeling bottleneck is real but solvable — especially if they land an academic partner (Mayo?)
- Ben Torres continues to be one of the strongest technical founders in our portfolio
- The competitive concern is Viz.ai's recent FDA clearance for cardiac AI. Luminary needs to move fast

Shared these notes with David. He agreed on all points — said we should offer to help connect them with potential academic data partners.

title: Luminary Health Partners with Mayo Clinic to Deploy AI Radiology Tools Across Rochester Campus
author: Christina Hall
content:
Luminary Health Partners with Mayo Clinic to Deploy AI Radiology Tools Across Rochester Campus
By Christina Hall | TechCrunch | May 19, 2026

Luminary Health, the San Francisco-based startup building AI-powered clinical decision support for radiologists, announced today a multi-year partnership with Mayo Clinic to deploy its platform across Mayo's Rochester, Minnesota campus.

The deal, which sources say is valued at nearly $500K annually with expansion rights to Mayo's Arizona and Florida locations, represents one of the largest AI radiology contracts signed by a Series A-stage company.

Mayo Clinic ran a pilot program with Luminary earlier this year, analyzing over 500 radiology studies. The results were striking: a 38% reduction in average read time with 99.2% concordance with radiologist diagnoses.

"We evaluated several AI radiology platforms, and Luminary stood out for how seamlessly it integrated into our radiologists' existing workflows," said Dr. Patricia Walsh, Chair of Radiology at Mayo Clinic. "Our radiologists didn't just tolerate the tool — they asked us to keep it."

Dr. Anika Sharma, CEO and co-founder of Luminary Health, said the Mayo partnership validates the company's approach of prioritizing clinician experience over pure algorithmic performance.

"Every AI radiology company can show you impressive accuracy numbers in a controlled setting," Sharma told TechCrunch. "What matters is whether radiologists actually use it during their 4 AM shifts when they're reading their 200th chest X-ray. That's the problem we solve."

Luminary Health was founded in 2023 by Sharma, a radiologist and former clinical AI researcher at Stanford, and CTO Ben Torres, previously an engineering lead at Google Health. The company raised a $12 million Series A led by AIVC in March 2025, following a $3 million seed round from Sequoia Scout.

The startup says it now serves 180 hospitals with $3.8 million in annual recurring revenue and is expanding into cardiology imaging, where it plans to launch a beta program later this year.

The AI radiology market has grown increasingly competitive, with well-funded players like Aidoc (which raised $75 million in February) and Viz.ai competing for health system contracts. But Luminary's workflow-first approach and the Mayo Clinic endorsement could help it punch above its weight class.

"Mayo doesn't partner with startups lightly," said one healthcare VC who asked not to be named. "This is a strong signal that Luminary's technology actually works in a real clinical environment."

Shares of public radiology companies were unaffected by the news. Luminary Health did not disclose the exact financial terms of the partnership.

title: AI in Medical Imaging: The Startups to Watch in 2026
author: Michael Rodriguez
content:
AI in Medical Imaging: The Startups to Watch in 2026
By Michael Rodriguez | Forbes | March 5, 2026

The AI medical imaging market is projected to reach $4.2 billion by 2028, and a new generation of startups is racing to capture it. As health systems grapple with radiologist shortages and exploding imaging volumes, AI-assisted diagnosis has moved from experimental curiosity to clinical necessity.

Here are five companies shaping the space in 2026.

Aidoc — The Category Leader
Tel Aviv-based Aidoc remains the most well-funded pure-play AI radiology company, with over $250 million raised to date. Its "always-on" AI platform analyzes medical images in real time and is deployed in more than 1,000 healthcare facilities globally. Aidoc's strength is breadth — it offers FDA-cleared algorithms across multiple pathologies, from pulmonary embolism to cervical spine fractures. The company raised $75 million in a Series C round in February 2026, citing plans to expand into new imaging modalities.

Viz.ai — The Stroke Pioneer
Viz.ai made its name with AI-powered stroke detection, cutting time-to-treatment by enabling faster identification of large vessel occlusions. The company has since expanded into cardiac and pulmonary imaging, recently securing FDA clearance for a cardiac AI module. Viz.ai's direct integration with hospital communication systems — alerting the right specialist instantly when a critical finding is detected — gives it a unique workflow advantage.

Luminary Health — The Workflow Innovator
The youngest company on this list, San Francisco-based Luminary Health has taken a different approach to the market. Rather than competing on algorithmic accuracy alone, Luminary focuses on integrating AI assistance into the radiologist's natural workflow. Founded by radiologist Dr. Anika Sharma and former Google Health engineer Ben Torres, the company claims its platform reduces read times by 40% — an efficiency metric that resonates with overworked radiology departments. Luminary raised a $12 million Series A from AIVC in 2025 and is reportedly in conversations with several major academic medical centers. With just $3M+ in ARR and fewer than 50 employees, it's early days, but the company's rapid hospital adoption suggests strong product-market fit.

Annalise.ai — The Global Player
Australian startup Annalise.ai has distinguished itself with the broadest set of findings detectable from a single chest X-ray — over 120 clinical findings. The company has gained traction in Europe and Asia-Pacific markets that many US-focused competitors have ignored.

Nanox — The Hardware Play
Nanox is taking a different approach entirely, combining AI software with affordable digital X-ray hardware designed for underserved markets. The company's vision of democratizing medical imaging in emerging economies could open a massive market that pure software plays can't easily access.

The Consolidation Question
With Databricks, Google, and Microsoft all signaling interest in healthcare AI, the question for these startups isn't just whether their technology works — it's whether they can build durable competitive advantages before the platform giants arrive. The companies that combine clinical validation, regulatory expertise, and deep health system relationships will likely be the survivors.

"The AI medical imaging market is going through the same cycle every enterprise software market goes through," said Dr. Sharma of Luminary Health. "There's a lot of noise right now, but eventually clinicians will choose the tools that actually make their lives better, not the ones with the best marketing."

title: Aidoc Raises $75M Series C to Expand AI Radiology Platform
author: Sarah Lehman
content:
Aidoc Raises $75M Series C to Expand AI Radiology Platform
By Sarah Lehman | Fierce Healthcare | February 11, 2026

Aidoc, the Tel Aviv-based AI radiology company, has raised $75 million in a Series C funding round led by General Catalyst, with participation from existing investors including TCV and Olive Tree Ventures. The round brings Aidoc's total funding to over $250 million.

The company said it will use the funds to expand its platform beyond radiology into new imaging modalities, deepen integrations with electronic health records, and grow its commercial team in the United States and Europe.

"We've proven that AI can be a reliable partner for radiologists," said Elad Walach, CEO of Aidoc. "Now we're expanding that partnership to every clinician who makes decisions based on medical images."

Aidoc's platform currently offers more than 20 FDA-cleared AI algorithms that analyze medical images in real time, flagging urgent findings like pulmonary embolism, intracranial hemorrhage, and cervical spine fractures. The company says its technology is deployed in over 1,000 healthcare facilities worldwide, including major US health systems.

The Series C comes as competition in the AI radiology market intensifies. Startups like Viz.ai, Luminary Health, and Annalise.ai are all vying for health system contracts, while larger technology companies are signaling increased interest in the space.

Industry analysts note that Aidoc's strategy of breadth — covering many pathologies rather than specializing in one — gives it an advantage in health system procurement, where buyers increasingly prefer platform solutions over point products.

"Aidoc is positioning itself as the default AI layer for radiology departments," said Dr. Nina Kottler, a radiology AI consultant. "The question is whether specialized players with deeper expertise in specific areas can offer enough differentiation to compete."

Aidoc reported that its annual recurring revenue exceeded $30 million in 2025, though the company declined to share specific growth figures. The company employs approximately 300 people across offices in Tel Aviv, New York, and London.

title: Viz.ai Announces FDA Clearance for Cardiac AI Module
author: Dave Muoio
content:
Viz.ai Announces FDA Clearance for Cardiac AI Module
By Dave Muoio | MobiHealthNews | April 7, 2026

Viz.ai, the AI-powered clinical intelligence company, announced today that it has received FDA 510(k) clearance for its cardiac AI module, which uses deep learning to analyze echocardiograms and identify structural heart abnormalities.

The clearance covers automated measurement of ejection fraction, detection of regional wall motion abnormalities, and identification of significant valvular disease — capabilities that could reduce the time cardiologists spend on routine echocardiogram interpretation.

"Cardiac imaging is the natural next frontier for AI in clinical care," said Chris Mansi, CEO of Viz.ai. "We've shown that AI can transform stroke care. Now we're bringing that same approach to the heart."

Viz.ai made its name with AI-powered stroke detection, where its technology is credited with reducing time-to-treatment by enabling faster identification of large vessel occlusions. The cardiac module extends the company's platform beyond neurovascular imaging into what industry analysts estimate is a $1.5 billion total addressable market for cardiac imaging AI.

The FDA clearance is based on a clinical validation study of 2,500 echocardiograms conducted at three academic medical centers. Viz.ai reported that its AI achieved 96.4% agreement with expert cardiologist reads for ejection fraction measurement and 93.8% sensitivity for detecting significant valvular abnormalities.

"This clearance is significant because it opens the door for AI-assisted cardiac imaging at scale," said Dr. Robert Califf, a cardiologist and health policy expert. "Echocardiography is one of the highest-volume cardiac tests, and anything that helps cardiologists work more efficiently could have real clinical impact."

Viz.ai said it plans to begin commercial rollout of the cardiac module in Q3 2026, initially targeting existing customers in its stroke detection network. The company has not disclosed pricing for the cardiac add-on.

The announcement could put pressure on other medical imaging AI companies that have signaled plans to expand into cardiac imaging, including Luminary Health and HeartFlow. The race to establish a dominant AI platform for cardiac imaging is expected to intensify through 2026.

Viz.ai has raised approximately $250 million in total funding and reports more than 1,200 hospitals on its stroke detection platform.

title: Luminary Health — Q1 2026 Investor Update

content:
From: Anika Sharma <anika@luminaryhealth.com>
To: investors@luminaryhealth.com
Date: April 5, 2026
Subject: Luminary Health — Q1 2026 Investor Update

Dear Investors,

I'm pleased to share our Q1 2026 update. It was a strong quarter for Luminary Health on multiple fronts.

Key Metrics (Q1 2026)
- ARR: $3.4M (up from $2.9M in Q4 2025, +17% QoQ)
- Net new hospitals: 22 (total: 168)
- Net Revenue Retention: 118%
- Monthly burn: $420K
- Cash on hand: $6.7M
- Runway: ~16 months
- Headcount: 42 (up from 39)

Highlights

Hospital growth accelerated in Q1, with 22 net new hospitals compared to 16 in Q4 2025. We're seeing increasing inbound interest as word-of-mouth from existing customers drives referrals. Our average deal size also increased to $22K ACV (up from $18K), reflecting a shift toward larger health system contracts.

Our expansion revenue continues to be strong at 118% NRR. This is driven by existing hospital customers adding departments and expanding the number of radiologists on the platform. The usage-based component of our pricing is working as intended — hospitals that start with a pilot naturally expand as more radiologists see the value.

Mayo Clinic is in active discussions with us about a campus-wide deployment. We ran a successful pilot in February (500 studies, 38% read time reduction, 99.2% concordance). I expect to have a signed contract by mid-Q2. This would be a landmark reference customer for us.

Product

We shipped v3.2 in February with an improved chest X-ray model that increased sensitivity by 4 percentage points. Customer feedback has been very positive.

On the roadmap, our cardiology module is in early prototype stage. Ben and the team are using transfer learning from our radiology models to accelerate development. We're targeting a beta program with 3-5 partner hospitals in Q3 2026. This represents a significant TAM expansion — we estimate that cardiology imaging adds $300-400K in potential ACV per large health system.

Concerns

VP Sales: This remains my top concern. I'm still the primary person selling, which is not sustainable as the company scales. We're actively searching for a VP Sales with enterprise health tech experience. Two candidates fell through in Q4, which was frustrating. David Okonkwo is helping with introductions from the AIVC network.

Competitive landscape: Aidoc raised $75M in February. They have significantly more resources than we do. Viz.ai received FDA clearance for a cardiac AI module in early April, which is relevant to our cardiology expansion plans. Our competitive advantage remains our workflow integration and radiologist UX — we're not trying to win on model accuracy alone.

Engineering bandwidth: We need 2 more ML engineers to support the cardiology expansion while maintaining momentum on our core radiology product.

Looking Ahead (Q2 2026)
- Close Mayo Clinic partnership
- Hire VP Sales
- Continue cardiology prototype development; secure 3 beta hospital partners
- Begin Series B positioning (targeting Q4 2026 / Q1 2027)

Thank you for your continued support. Happy to discuss any questions.

Best,
Anika Sharma
CEO, Luminary Health
